rows.name: Reusable agent skills
rows.offer: Agents discover project-level and global skill files and invoke them on their own when a task fits.

text.contains: flisk project` writes the Flisk skills to `.claude/skills/`

rows.name: Project rules via AGENTS.md
rows.offer: Agents read an AGENTS.md at the repo root and in subdirectories as standing project rules.

rows.name: MCP servers for agents
rows.offer: The app lets users register MCP servers over streamable HTTP or SSE so local agents gain extra tools and data.

flisk.reason: Flisk is the MCP server side (flisk mcp plus hosted --type mcp resources) and documents client setup per agent host, but it ships no client-side server registry or UI.

rows.name: Agent watches live dev server
rows.offer: The agent attaches to a running dev server, database shell or debugger, reads its live output and reacts to it.

flisk.reason: An agent can read recent logs and status over MCP, but only as a bounded snapshot; there is no follow or stream tool.

rows.name: Programmatic API for runs
rows.offer: A public HTTP API, OpenAPI spec and CLI let scripts and CI start, monitor and cancel agent runs.

flisk.reason: Flisk is driven locally through a documented --json CLI envelope and the MCP tools; there is deliberately no network API for a single-machine runtime.

rows.name: Declarative definition in the repo
rows.offer: The whole setup is a versioned tree of YAML and Markdown files that can live in the user's own repository.

rows.name: Secret redaction in output
rows.offer: Configured patterns mask passwords, keys and PII before content is shown or sent to an LLM provider.

text.contains: Values from the project `.env` are redacted from output

rows.name: Secrets from external managers
rows.offer: Environment variables can pull dynamic secrets from managers such as 1Password, LastPass or HashiCorp Vault instead of storing values.

flisk.reason: Flisk reads secrets only from the project .env; a developer whose secrets live in a manager has to export them by hand before flisk up.

rows.acceptance: docs/environment.md documents a resolver (for example a command or op:// reference named in service.json secrets) and a test in cli/src proves flisk up injects the resolved value without writing it to a generated file.

ice.basis: Impact 5: teams with a secret manager are common but .env works for most local stacks. Confidence 5: Warp's page describes the user need but not how many users rely on it. Ease 4: secrets flow through cli/src/utils env handling and Compose injection, so a resolver touches the env pipeline and needs careful tests.

rows.name: Parallel stacks per git worktree
rows.offer: Several branches checked out as git worktrees each get their own agent and review context so parallel agents do not collide.

flisk.reason: Agents working in parallel worktrees need an isolated stack each, which Flisk cannot give today because ports, identity and discovery assume one instance per machine.

rows.acceptance: A command or flag (for example flisk up --instance <name>) plus a docs/ page and an e2e test under tests/e2e starting the same project twice from two worktrees without port or name clashes; flisk status reports both.

ice.basis: Impact 7: running several coding agents on one repo is the launch audience's growing pain and the stack is what collides. Confidence 6: Warp pitches worktrees for parallel agents and docs/compare-honest.md lists multi-instance as an open design question. Ease 3: ports, Traefik hostnames and the registry in runtime/ all assume a single instance.

rows.name: Per-agent tool permission profiles
rows.offer: Profiles set how autonomous an agent is, which commands run unprompted and which MCP servers it may call.

flisk.reason: The flisk mcp server exposes mutating tools (down, config_regenerate, resource_create) with no read-only mode, so a user cannot give an agent inspect-only access to the stack.

rows.acceptance: A flag or env var (for example flisk mcp --read-only) hides or refuses the mutating tools in cli/src/mcp/tools.ts, covered by a test in cli/src/mcp/__tests__ and described in docs/mcp.md.

ice.basis: Impact 5: safe-by-default agent access is a recurring ask but agent hosts already gate tool calls. Confidence 6: Warp documents per-profile MCP rules and Flisk's tool list is known to be partly destructive. Ease 7: the tools are declared in one file (cli/src/mcp/tools.ts), so filtering by a flag is a small change in an existing place.

rows.name: Cloud agent environments
rows.offer: Hosted cloud agents run in a repeatable container with set repositories and setup commands on every run.

flisk.reason: Hosted cloud workspaces are a different product; Flisk runs the user's own stack on their own machine.

rows.name: Scheduled cloud agents
rows.offer: Cloud agents run on a cron schedule for chores such as dependency upkeep and issue triage.

flisk.reason: A hosted scheduler for agent runs belongs to a control plane; Flisk only runs the local stack while the developer works.

rows.name: Parent and child agent runs
rows.offer: A parent agent spawns child agents, locally or in the cloud, and the user inspects every conversation and artifact.

flisk.reason: Scheduling LLM agents is the agent framework's job; Flisk hosts the agent processes and their services, not their plans.

rows.name: Live agent session sharing
rows.offer: Collaborators can watch, steer and reply inside a live agent session from another device.

flisk.reason: Sharing a terminal or agent view is a workspace feature; Flisk is a local CLI with no shared session surface.

rows.name: Trigger agents from Slack and Linear
rows.offer: Agents start from Slack, Linear, Jira or GitHub events and report back there.

flisk.reason: Event-driven cloud triggers need a hosted service; a local runtime has no inbound audience for them.

rows.name: SSO for the workspace
rows.offer: Organisations sign users in through Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace or any SAML or OIDC provider.

flisk.reason: Flisk has no accounts or hosted workspace to sign in to; it is a local MIT CLI.

rows.name: Bring your own model key
rows.offer: Users plug in their own Anthropic, OpenAI or Google keys to control model choice, billing and data routing.

flisk.reason: Flisk does not call models itself; the agent in the user's service or editor owns model access.

rows.name: Self-hosted cloud agent workers
rows.offer: An enterprise plan runs cloud agent workloads on the customer's own compute while Warp tracks each run.

flisk.reason: Flisk has no cloud control plane to point at customer compute, and stays a single-machine local runtime.

rows.name: Hand a local agent to the cloud
rows.offer: An in-progress local agent conversation and uncommitted changes are snapshotted and continued as a cloud run.

flisk.reason: Moving work to hosted agents needs a cloud runner, which a local-only runtime does not provide.

rows.name: Agent GUI testing with recordings
rows.offer: Agents drive a desktop GUI in a sandbox and return an annotated video as proof of a change.

flisk.reason: Desktop GUI automation is an agent capability; Flisk supplies the running app and its health, not the test driver.

rows.name: Saved parameterised commands
rows.offer: Named commands with arguments are saved, searched in a palette and shared with the team.

flisk.reason: A command library is a terminal-emulator feature; Flisk's own commands are the shell commands the user already types.

rows.name: Restore windows and panes
rows.offer: Windows, tabs, panes and recent blocks come back when the terminal app restarts.

flisk.reason: Restoring terminal layout is a terminal-emulator concern; Flisk restores services with flisk up, not UI state.

rows.name: Codebase context indexing
rows.offer: The app indexes a git repository locally so agents answer with real knowledge of the code.

flisk.reason: Code search and indexing belong to the agent host; Flisk gives agents stack state, not code understanding.

rows.name: LLM scorers for agent runs
rows.offer: An LLM-based evaluation grades completed agent runs against criteria the team defines.

flisk.reason: Grading hosted agent runs needs run history on a platform; Flisk's observability is local logs, status and doctor.
